A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same polytope-based kernel calibration work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D support comparison, including matching renamed methods and reorganized figures.

before.justification: Sections 6.1-6.2 report original experiments on five simulations and 46 OpenML-CC18 datasets, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: Sections 6.1-6.3 report original simulation, OpenML, and ResNet-20 vision experiments, including calibration and OOD detection outcomes.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming KGF/KGN to KDF/KDN, v6 introduces kernel-derived geodesic distance for kernel selection. Section 5.1 replaces covariance estimation using weighted neighboring-polytope samples with within-polytope estimation. Weight exponents also change from fixed schedules to k log n with held-out selection of k.

E1.justification: The original five simulations remain, and Trunk adds coverage of increasing dimension. V6 adds CIFAR-10-trained vision evaluation on CIFAR-100, SVHN, and noise, introducing near- and far-OOD scenarios beyond the earlier OpenML experiments. OpenML coverage decreases from 46 to 45 datasets through the stated exclusion of dataset 23517.

E2.justification: V5 compares the proposed methods with their RF and neural-network parents. V6 adds isotonic and sigmoid calibration to the corresponding OpenML comparisons in Figure 2 and Appendix Figures 4-7. The new vision comparison also evaluates ACET alongside the parent and both calibration baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6 replaces adaptive calibration error with maximum calibration error, retaining 15 bins, and changes OCE from an absolute difference after averaging to an average absolute deviation. Benchmark summaries switch from differences to normalized improvements. Added protocols include a 90/10 fitting/calibration split, AUROC/FPR@95 reporting, and a Trunk dimension sweep with 5000 training samples and OOD radius 20.

E4.justification: V6 expands parent-versus-kernel comparisons into explicit Euclidean-versus-geodesic comparisons for both model families. The Trunk dimension sweep tests sensitivity to increasing dimension in Figure 1, while Appendix Figure 3 adds posterior visualizations for the distance variants. These are new analyses, beyond relocating earlier simulation displays.

E5.justification: V6 first specifies 45 simulation repetitions and adds directional Wilcoxon rank-sum tests comparing final-sample improvements across datasets in Figure 2. Median and 25th/75th percentile reporting remain. The PDFs do not establish that the number of repetitions increased.

E6.justification: V6 replaces benchmark curves under revised methods and metrics and adds results for calibration baselines, distance variants, Trunk, and vision tests. New Table 1 reports KDN CIFAR-10 accuracy/MCE of 83.60%/0.02 versus the parent's 83.70%/0.13, but CIFAR-100 AUROC of 0.69 versus 0.78. These are new within-v6 comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v5.

T1.justification: V6 adds Corollaries 4-5 asserting suitable forest/network partition classes and Corollary 6 establishing the proposed polytope distance as a metric, with proof arguments in Appendix A.3-A.5. Theorem 1 tightens the bandwidth factor from at most 1 to strictly below 1, and Appendix A.1 revises the Dirac-delta unbiasedness argument. Distance and OCE definitions also change.

C1.justification: The joint ID/OOD calibration and conditional consistency contributions remain. V6 refocuses the abstract from bridging discriminative and generative approaches toward calibration while mostly preserving or improving accuracy, explicitly contrasting this with post-hoc calibrators. The Discussion similarly changes accuracy 'close to' the parent into 'similar to or better than' it.

C2.justification: V5 emphasizes Euclidean-distance limitations and defers geodesic/CNN benchmarking. V6 explains the geodesic distance's finite polytope resolution and interprets vision results as a compromise between ID and OOD calibration. Section 6.3 newly identifies near-OOD performance as unresolved and discusses known outliers or alternative kernels as possible remedies.

D1.justification: V6 newly specifies 1000 training samples for the ordinary simulation OOD tests, documents the Trunk generator and settings, and identifies ResNet-20 for vision experiments. Fixed exponent defaults disappear from the hyperparameter tables in favor of held-out grid search, without a stated search range. Hardware/software details remain, and Algorithm 1 still describes weighted MLE despite the revised covariance equation.

R1.justification: V6 adds references supporting isotonic/sigmoid calibration, kernel distances, Trunk, near-OOD discussion, and consistency/approximation arguments. It removes the Nguyen/Sehwag adversarial-evasion discussion and the Nixon and Madhyastha references. Section 2's central positioning against Ren, Wan, and Meinke remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract is substantially rewritten, Generative terminology becomes Density, and author order changes. Parameter estimation is reorganized into separate covariance and sample-ratio subsections. The experimental narrative is extensively reworked into simulation, OpenML, and vision studies, while the Discussion is shortened and limitations are developed in Section 6.3.

P2.justification: V5 Figure 1 becomes the expanded, transposed appendix Figure 3. Simulation plots gain panels and distance variants; the OpenML summary gains baseline curves and statistical annotations; a vision-results table is added. Six OpenML appendix figures become four displays grouping metrics and model families by dataset, with dataset IDs replacing earlier name/sample/feature/class annotations.

improvement.justification: V6 addresses v5's explicitly deferred comparison with calibration methods and CNN-based image experiments through the expanded OpenML comparisons and vision Table 1. Distance-variant and dimensionality analyses substantially strengthen empirical support, while the near-OOD discussion exposes an important applicability limit. Reproducibility remains imperfect, particularly the unspecified tuning grid and covariance/pseudocode inconsistency, but these do not outweigh the substantial gains in comparative evidence.
